articles.title: Farmers in India call for another national mobilization
articles.author: Abdul Rahman
articles.content_excerpt: Farmers unions in India, under the banner of the Samyukta Kisan Morcha (SKM), have called for a nationwide mobilization to protest the attempt to open the country’s agricultural market for foreign competition without addressing the problems they’ve been facing for years. The protests will mark the sixth anniversary of the 2020-21 protests, in which thousands of farmers had camped on the borders of the capital, New Delhi, for months, forcing the government to withdraw farm laws and promise to address other agricultural issues. articles.title: France’s protest movement is fighting more than Macron
articles.author: Rania Khalek
articles.content_excerpt: Macron offered “crumbs.” France answered with a general strike against austerity that brought the country to a standstill and more than 1.6 million people to the streets. Iman D., a student organizer with the Party for Socialism and Liberation, was on the ground at the Paris protests. She tells Zoe Alexandra and Rania Khalek the multinational, multigenerational movement behind the shutdown names capitalism as the problem, not just Emmanuel Macron and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu. Iman explains why Nov. 5 general strikers carried Palestinian flags and wore keffiyehs, and unpacks how Black and Arab youth from the suburbs – the children and grandchildren of the people France colonized – helped spark the uprising. articles.title: General strike brings Spain to a halt
articles.author: Ana Vračar
articles.content_excerpt: Hundreds of thousands of workers in key sectors – with total participation likely in the millions – responded to a general strike call in Spain on Wednesday, November 11, demanding solutions to the housing crisis and protection of labor rights. The action represents the first nationwide work stoppage in 14 years. The strike was called by the country’s largest trade unions – the General Union of Workers (Unión General de Trabajadores, UGT) and the Workers’ Commissions (Comisiones Obreras) – alongside tenants associations and other unions, including the General Confederation of Labor (Confederación General del Trabajo, CGT). articles.title: Outrage and anger in Paraguay: a new president is sworn in, but there is no relief
articles.author: Pablo Meriguet
articles.content_excerpt: Although many had hoped Santiago Peña’s resignation as president of Paraguay would calm the anger of millions of Paraguayans, it did not. As the hours pass, hundreds of protesters are joining spontaneous demonstrations against Paraguay’s political and economic establishment. And the truth is, this comes as no surprise. It has been revealed that Ueno Bank was a financial institution that grew rapidly thanks to contributions from pensioners and other state-linked sources that Peña’s own government ordered to be injected into a bank that had only just been officially recognized as such in 2023. articles.title: Meet David Morales: Providence Voters Elect Democratic Socialist Mayor, Approve Israel Divestment
articles.content_excerpt: Voters in Providence, Rhode Island, approved a ballot measure last week that could result in the city divesting from Israel. The successful grassroots campaign makes Providence the first U.S. city to pass a binding divestment measure through a popular vote. The measure instructs the city to divest from countries and companies implicated in “ethnic cleansing, apartheid, illegal military occupation, or genocide.” The language does not mention Israel by name. articles.title: “Birds of War”: New Film Tells a Story of Love and Journalism from Syria to Lebanon
articles.content_excerpt: We speak with Janay Boulos and Abd Alkader Habak, filmmakers and subjects of the new documentary Birds of War , which tells their epic love story through years of upheaval in the Middle East. articles.title: Yet another catastrophic winter in Gaza
articles.author: Aseel Saleh
articles.content_excerpt: For the fourth consecutive year, and more than a year after the US-brokered ceasefire deal was reached, Palestinian people in Gaza continue to suffer from a severe humanitarian crisis caused by extreme weather conditions amid ongoing Israeli assaults and restrictions. On Sunday, November 8, a steep sand dune collapsed onto tents sheltering displaced people in Deir al-Balah in the central Gaza Strip, killing five people , including four children and a woman. A number of other injured people were rescued from the site, according to media reports. A report issued by the United Nations International Children’s Emergency Fund (UNICEF) on Monday, November 9, revealed that the catastrophic weather conditions have affected over 106,000 people in the besieged enclave.
